knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ parametrized by $\mathbf r(u,v)$ for $D=(0,1)\times(0,1)$, where

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\left\langle x y,\,- x,\,3 z\right\rangle.
$$

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\left\langle u,\,v,\,2 u v\right\rangle.
$$

Orient $S$ so that its unit normal has a **negative $z$-component**.

If

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D ?\,\mathrm dA,
$$

what is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The vector area element must agree with the specified orientation. First compute the tangent vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u & =\left\langle 1,\,0,\,2 v\right\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v & =\left\langle 0,\,1,\,2 u\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Their ordered cross product is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1&0&2 v\\0&1&2 u\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left\langle - 2 v,\,- 2 u,\,1\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Its $z$-component is positive. Reverse this direction to satisfy the stated orientation:

$$
\mathbf N=-(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)=\left\langle 2 v,\,2 u,\,-1\right\rangle.
$$

For this orientation,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N(u,v)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Substitute $x=u$, $y=v$, $z=2 u v$ into the field:

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\left\langle u v,\,- u,\,6 u v\right\rangle.
$$

Compute the three component contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{x} & =\left(u v\right)\left(2 v\right) \\  & =2 u v^{2} \\ T_{y} & =\left(- u\right)\left(2 u\right) \\  & =- 2 u^{2} \\ T_{z} & =\left(6 u v\right)\left(-1\right) \\  & =- 6 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Take the dot product component by component:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf N & =T_x+T_y+T_z \\  & =- 2 u^{2} + 2 u v^{2} - 6 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\left(- 2 u^{2} + 2 u v^{2} - 6 u v\right)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ parametrized by $\mathbf r(u,v)$ for $D=(0,1)\times(0,1)$, where

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\left\langle 3 z,\,- y,\,- 3 x z\right\rangle.
$$

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\left\langle v,\,- u v,\,u\right\rangle.
$$

Orient $S$ so that its unit normal has a **negative $y$-component**.

If

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D ?\,\mathrm dA,
$$

what is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The vector area element must agree with the specified orientation. First compute the tangent vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u & =\left\langle 0,\,- v,\,1\right\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v & =\left\langle 1,\,- u,\,0\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Their ordered cross product is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\0&- v&1\\1&- u&0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left\langle u,\,1,\,v\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Its $y$-component is positive. Reverse this direction to satisfy the stated orientation:

$$
\mathbf N=-(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)=\left\langle - u,\,-1,\,- v\right\rangle.
$$

For this orientation,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N(u,v)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Substitute $x=v$, $y=- u v$, $z=u$ into the field:

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\left\langle 3 u,\,u v,\,- 3 u v\right\rangle.
$$

Compute the three component contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{x} & =\left(3 u\right)\left(- u\right) \\  & =- 3 u^{2} \\ T_{y} & =\left(u v\right)\left(-1\right) \\  & =- u v \\ T_{z} & =\left(- 3 u v\right)\left(- v\right) \\  & =3 u v^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Take the dot product component by component:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf N & =T_x+T_y+T_z \\  & =- 3 u^{2} + 3 u v^{2} - u v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\left(- 3 u^{2} + 3 u v^{2} - u v\right)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ parametrized by $\mathbf r(u,v)$ for $D=(0,1)\times(0,1)$, where

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\left\langle 3 z,\,- y,\,2 x z\right\rangle.
$$

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\left\langle v,\,u v,\,u\right\rangle.
$$

Orient $S$ so that its unit normal has a **negative $y$-component**.

If

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D ?\,\mathrm dA,
$$

what is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The vector area element must agree with the specified orientation. First compute the tangent vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u & =\left\langle 0,\,v,\,1\right\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v & =\left\langle 1,\,u,\,0\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Their ordered cross product is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\0&v&1\\1&u&0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left\langle - u,\,1,\,- v\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Its $y$-component is positive. Reverse this direction to satisfy the stated orientation:

$$
\mathbf N=-(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)=\left\langle u,\,-1,\,v\right\rangle.
$$

For this orientation,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N(u,v)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Substitute $x=v$, $y=u v$, $z=u$ into the field:

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\left\langle 3 u,\,- u v,\,2 u v\right\rangle.
$$

Compute the three component contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{x} & =\left(3 u\right)\left(u\right) \\  & =3 u^{2} \\ T_{y} & =\left(- u v\right)\left(-1\right) \\  & =u v \\ T_{z} & =\left(2 u v\right)\left(v\right) \\  & =2 u v^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Take the dot product component by component:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf N & =T_x+T_y+T_z \\  & =3 u^{2} + 2 u v^{2} + u v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\left(3 u^{2} + 2 u v^{2} + u v\right)\,\mathrm dA.
$$
